verdict.headline: Wholesale prices jump the most since 2022, yet yields fall as money rotates from chips into the Dow
verdict.label: Close: S&P 500 7,744.06 (+0.33%) after an intraday low near 7,670, four points above 7,666.45; Dow 52,177.69 (+1.08%); Russell 2000 +1.38%; Nasdaq 26,713.03 (+0.08%); chips -0.88%; 10Y ~5.10% (about -10 bp); October hike odds ~32%; BTC $82,237 after a $79,688 low.
verdict.rationale_short: September PPI rose 1.3% on the month and 6.3% on the year, the largest annual gain since December 2022, with energy behind over 80% of it; retail sales beat at 0.8% but the control group rose only 0.1%. The ten-year still fell about 10 basis points to roughly 5.10% and October hike odds held near 32%, so the hot print moved neither yields nor the Fed path. Stocks split the same way: the S&P 500 fell to about 7,670, four points above 7,666.45, then closed up 0.33%, while the Dow rose 1.08%, the Russell 2000 1.38% and the chip index fell another 0.88%. CoreWeave reversed a 9.5% drop to close up 5.94% after Jensen Huang said its cost of capital is falling. This morning's read that the selling is about AI financing and valuation rather than rates held up; its worry about 7,666.45 did not. Warsh speaks tonight in Bangkok; a close under 7,666.45 would show the rotation turning into broad selling.
verdict.lede_short: Producer prices rose 6.3% on the year, the most since 2022, and Treasury yields fell anyway as investors sold chip stocks and bought bonds. The S&P 500 dipped to within four points of 7,666 and closed up 0.3%, with the Dow up 1.1% while chips fell again, so the AI selling is rotating money within the market, not out of it. Fed Chair Warsh speaks tonight; a close under 7,666 would mean the selling had spread.

supporting_data.label: Producer prices rose 1.3% in September and 6.3% on the year, the most since December 2022, with energy over 80% of the gain — but the measure excluding food, energy and trade is at 5.0%, so the pressure is not only oil.
The ten-year fell about 10 basis points to roughly 5.10% and October hike odds stayed near 32% after the PPI — a hot inflation print that moved neither yields nor the Fed path.
Retail sales rose 0.8% against 0.3% expected, but the control group rose only 0.1% — households are paying more for fuel and spending less on everything else.
The Dow rose 1.08% to 52,177.69 and the Russell 2000 1.38% while Nvidia fell 1.84% — money left AI hardware for the rest of the market rather than leaving stocks.
Jensen Huang said CoreWeave's cost of capital is falling and it needs no backstop, after its default insurance hit a record 1,194.5 basis points — the stock reversed a 9.5% drop to close up 5.94%.
WTI rose about 3% to $97.97 on an 8-million-barrel inventory draw and Hormuz shipping attacks, while Brent settled at $105.92 — energy already drove over 80% of September's PPI gain.

watchlist_mentions.note: Fell 1.84% as chips fell again; Huang said CoreWeave's cost of capital is decreasing and it needs no Nvidia backstop.
Reversed a 9.5% morning drop to close up 5.94% after Huang's remarks; five-year default insurance had hit a record 1,194.5 basis points.
Reports Wednesday October 21 after the close — the first US megacap report since the AI sell-off began.
Fell to $79,688 on Crypto.com, below last week's $80,320 low, before recovering to $82,237.

trade_setups.thesis: The index held 7,666.45 intraday by about four points on a 6.3% PPI and closed 78 points above it, with the Dow and small caps rising while chips fell — a rotation within the market rather than broad selling.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close below 7,666.45 would show the selling spreading beyond AI and chips
trade_setups.horizon: Through Friday's options expiry and Warsh's remarks

trade_setups.thesis: Shares rebounded 5.94% after Huang's comments while five-year default insurance sat near a record 1,194.5 basis points; whether the spread follows the stock decides whether the rebound has lenders behind it.
trade_setups.invalidation: Spread narrowing with the stock would confirm; shares holding while the spread stays near the record would leave the rebound resting on comments

trade_setups.thesis: Yields fell about 10 basis points on a hot PPI as investors bought bonds with proceeds from chip sales; Warsh's Bangkok remarks test whether that holds if October hike odds rise from 32%.
trade_setups.invalidation: Hike odds back above 45% with the ten-year rising toward 5.331% would end the safety bid
